senses.gloss:
bāṇaliṅga
(‘liṅga of बाण’)
------------------------------------------
Bāṇaliṅgas are natural liṅgas of शिव (svayambhū or self-manifest) made of crystallized quartz, and generally found in some sacred rivers like the नर्मदा. A legend goes that शिव got them manifested at the special request of Bāṇāsura, a great devotee of his; hence the name ‘bāṇaliṅga’.
Though several stones shaped like a लिङ्ग are found in the river नर्मदा, not all of them are bāṇaliṅgas. Special charac-teristics are prescribed for them by noting which one can discover a true बाणलिङ्ग.
The bāṇaliṅgas occur in many shapes and sizes as also colours. They are hence given different names. The ‘āgneya-लिङ्ग’ will be rose in colour and warm to touch. The ‘yāmya-लिङ्ग’ is shaped like a cudgel whereas the ‘varuṇa-लिङ्ग’ is round in shape. The ‘raudra-लिङ्ग’ resembles a bone-piece. The ‘vaiṣṇava-लिङ्ग’ has varie-gated colours. They are sometimes given different names of Śiva—like Svayambhū, Mṛtyuñjaya or Nīlakaṇṭha—depending upon their external characteristics.

Bāṇa
------------------------------------------
Bāṇa or Bāṇāsura was the eldest son of the demon king बलि. He was a great devotee of Lord शिव and had obtained several boons from him. अनिरुद्ध, the grandson of कृष्ण, had surreptitiously married बाण’s daughter Uṣā at her request. This led to a war between कृष्ण and बाण in which the latter was defeated.
Bāṇa is also the name of another asura or demon who had constructed three flying cities. At the behest of the gods like इन्द्र, शिव spared his life and permitted him to live in the Svarṇapura (the golden city).
